title: Detect a UTF-8 Byte-Order Mark in Saved Text
goal: Read one UTF-8 file or standard input and report whether its first three bytes are the UTF-8 byte-order mark, plus the total byte count. Validate the entire input as UTF-8; treat it as read-only data and do not modify or execute it.
intro: A UTF-8 byte-order mark (BOM) is optional, but some downstream text tools handle it differently. This small CLI checks only whether the input begins with the exact UTF-8 BOM bytes (`EF BB BF`) and reports the byte length. It reads the data without changing it and rejects invalid UTF-8.
requirements: Standard library only; no external crates, unsafe code, include macros, environment variables, subprocesses, networking, or filesystem writes.
Accept exactly one CLI argument: a local UTF-8 file path or `-` for standard input.
Read all bytes, reject invalid UTF-8, and report total byte count and whether the first three bytes are exactly the UTF-8 BOM.
Write successful results to stdout and actionable failures to stderr; use a nonzero exit only on failure.
Treat all input as untrusted text and never execute or alter it.
limits: The program reads the entire input into memory, so it is intended for reasonably sized saved text.
It reports only whether the exact UTF-8 BOM byte sequence is at offset zero; it does not detect other encodings or BOM-like bytes elsewhere.
A BOM is valid UTF-8 and remains part of the reported byte count.
No execution or test results are claimed here.
steps: Create a synthetic UTF-8 input whose bytes are `EF BB BF 68 69 0A`.
Run `./recipe sample.txt` and compare stdout with the exact expected output.
Also try `./recipe -` with the same bytes on stdin, a file without a BOM, invalid UTF-8, a missing path, and an incorrect number of arguments; confirm failures are actionable and go to stderr.
checks: Compile using the stated Rust 2021 command.
For bytes `EF BB BF 68 69 0A`, verify stdout is exactly `bytes: 6` followed by `utf8_bom: yes`.
For UTF-8 bytes `68 69 0A`, verify stdout reports `bytes: 3` and `utf8_bom: no`.
For malformed UTF-8, verify the program exits nonzero and reports the validation failure on stderr.
Verify a missing file and incorrect argument counts produce actionable stderr messages and do not create or change files.
usage: Intended runner: Rust 1.90.0, edition 2021. Compile with `rustc --edition=2021 recipe.rs -o recipe`. Run `./recipe <file>` to inspect a file, or `./recipe -` and provide text on standard input. Exactly one argument is required. Read and validation failures are written to stderr with a nonzero exit status; successful counts go to stdout.
example_input: Synthetic input file bytes: `EF BB BF 68 69 0A` (UTF-8 text containing a BOM followed by `hi` and a newline).
tested_scope: Executed 5 synthetic local fixture cases in isolated Rust 1.90.0 on GitHub Actions, without network access. Declared exit codes, output assertions and input integrity checks passed. Live services, installed third-party packages and production behavior remain outside scope. Editorial approval is still required.
